what: What a steady stream through the Kafka port costs the lake's bucket: requests a second by the class S3 and R2 bill them in, and dollars a month at list prices (S3: PUT/COPY/POST/LIST $5 a million, GET $0.40, storage $0.023 a GB-month; R2: class A $4.50, class B $0.36, $0.015 a GB-month; DELETE free). Requests from the simulator's own count (sim_r2.py `ops`), which the nodes' pondra_object_requests_total matched within 0.5%.
command: python3 tools/kafka_bench.py --s3 --steady 30 --nodes N --producers P --warm 30 --secs 90 (sim_r2.py with MOTO_S3_DEFAULT_KEY_BUFFER_SIZE=2000000000 --trace; PONDRA_CACHE_GB=3)
machine: one 4-core, 16 GB VM: the nodes, the simulator (Python, one core at 90%) and the producers (16 to 24 Python processes) shared its cores, which were all busy: the target 30 MiB/s was reached by none of the runs (14 to 26 MiB/s). limits-r2.yml's cost job measures it on real R2 nightly.

1 node, R2's latency.latency: R2's (sim_r2.py defaults: PUT p50 197 ms, GET p50 100 ms)

3 nodes, R2's latency.latency: R2's (sim_r2.py defaults: PUT p50 197 ms, GET p50 100 ms)

notes: Requests come per commit round, not per byte: one node at R2's latency made 10.9 writes a second at 6 MiB/s (4 producers) and 8.7 at 13 MiB/s (16 producers). Each round a node writes one log segment and the leader one catalog write-ahead-log object; a round lasts about as long as the bucket takes to answer, so a faster bucket means more rounds (S3's latency: 16 writes a second at 26 MiB/s).

Three nodes write a segment each a round: 10.8 segment writes a second, against one node's 4.6 at R2's latency and 10.3 at S3's. Followers also read every segment another node wrote (21.8 reads a second), to keep their SSD tiers warm; reads are a twelfth of a write's price.
The catalog (SlateDB) reads its manifest and garbage-collection marks about 2 to 5 times a second per node; at 100 nodes that would be about $500 a month on S3.

Tiering fell behind at 26 MiB/s on the saturated VM ('slow tiering: 1,061,958 rows in 49.8 s'), so the S3-latency run's Parquet writes (0.04 a second) are fewer than a machine with cores to spare would make (the R2 runs: 0.09 to 0.11 a second).

Kept: 678 bytes a row of about 1,050 bytes of values (LZ4 Parquet over words drawn from 2,048 made-up ones). At 30 MiB/s that is 1.9 TB a day: $43 a month on S3 for each day kept, the same in any system that keeps those bytes in a bucket.
OpenData's page puts Buffer at about $91 a month at 30 MB/s (16.2 M PUTs, about 6.25 writes a second), WarpStream at about $1,300 and self-hosted Kafka at about $8,500 (unverified).

unflushed: values the producers still held when they stopped (they offered more than the saturated VM took in). exactly_once counts what was acknowledged: every acknowledged value is in the table once, and nothing beyond what was sent.
by_object: Writes and reads a second by the object they went to, from sim_r2.py's --trace over 45 s inside the measured window (45 to 90 s after the run started); they add to within a few percent of the measured totals.
